title: The Tidemark Sails
description: Six flattened, keeled limestone ribs fan out over a shared stepped foundation.

review.notes: Round 2. Fixed: blocks are longer and vary in length, joints are fine recesses instead of pillow bulges, rib widths differ, rib backs have a crest, the full-surface grey mottling is gone. Builder's close call (blade thickness): the free tips are now thicker with rounded ends, but every rib still curls into a thin tapering hook, so the fan of six still reads as a grass tuft rather than one or two dominant ribs (round-1 point 2); close one or two ribs into arches or end them in a heavy capstone. Not fixed: (1) the 80 m ribs still stand on a low 4-step plinth, each on a ~1.5 m block; there are no massive root bodies and no walkable opening near the figure (round-1 point 3). (2) The material is uniformly clean with a sandpaper grain everywhere and no localized weathering at the rib feet or joints; the joints show as orange-brown gaps. (3) The scale figure is still barely findable on the sheet.
